g.text: Benjamini–Hochberg: controlling the false discovery rate

text.style: font-size: 13.5px; font-family: 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: middle; fill: #555555

g.text: Find the LARGEST k with p₍ₖ₎ ≤ (k/m)·q, then reject the k smallest p-values

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 13px; font-family: 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: middle; fill: #222222

g.text: BH keeps the AVERAGE share of false discoveries near q, and in return finds about twice as many real effects.

text.style: font-size: 12.5px; font-family: 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: middle; fill: #555555

g.text: It often makes at least one false discovery (high FWER). That is the trade-off FDR control accepts.
